LOS ANGELES, California (CNN)  -- It was a night for neon pink bow ties and words like "disaster" and "monstrosity." It was not the night, however, to be Paris Hilton, Mike Myers or Uwe Boll. Paula Einstein, Rebecca Marcotte and Kelie McIver do a parody of "Dancing Queen" to open the show. The 29th Annual Golden Raspberry Awards honored the worst film achievements of the year in a small theater in Hollywood on February 21. The night opened with a parody of the "Mamma Mia" song, "Dancing Queen," and ended with "Love Guru" being named worst picture. "It wasn't just the economy that tanked, so did the qualities of the movies being offered," Razzie founder John Wilson told CNN several weeks before the show. "I would suggest putting away all sharp [instruments] before putting the DVDs in your machine." Paris Hilton and Mike Myers came out on top -- or bottom -- for the awards. Hilton earned both the worst actress and worst supporting actress awards for her roles in "Hottie & the Nottie" and "Repo: The Genetic Opera." She was also awarded worst screen couple for her on-screen time with her co-stars Christine Lakin and Joel David Moore. Razzie host Gretchen Enders said that "Hottie & the Nottie" was "a vanity production in the worst sense... Hilton, who served as executive producer, has no one to blame but herself." Hilton's film had a budget of $2 million but only earned about $27,000 at the box office. "Under Obama's new plan, they wouldn't even have to pay taxes," Wilson deadpanned. Myers added worst actor to the "Love Guru" worst picture and worst screenplay Razzies. To save anyone else from having to watch it, Wilson shredded a DVD copy of the film on stage. Parody films "Disaster Movie" and "Meet the Spartans," each nominated in five categories, came away empty-handed. However, that doesn't mean the Razzie foundation thinks they were worthwhile. "When you invest the kind of money that a mainstream, big-budget star film requires, you want some insurance that your investment is going to come back to you. So... you're going to do what worked before," Wilson said. "Financially that may make sense, but in terms of the audience's enjoyment, surprise or appreciation of what you're doing, it doesn't work." Enter "Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull," this year's winner of the worst prequel, remake, rip-off or sequel award. "A fourth installment of a beloved franchise, but this one found itself loved by almost no one," hosts Katsy Chappell and Josh Thoemke said. The approximately 740 voting members of the Raspberry Foundation also found Pierce Brosnan's singing voice sorely lacking. His role in "Mama Mia" earned him the worst supporting actor award. "An actor who could not sing, should not sing and arguably did not sing, in a role he should not have accepted," Razzie hosts Chip Dornell and Kelie McIver said about the former James Bond. But perhaps the biggest "winner" of the night was Uwe Boll. Recipient of the worst director award, the foundation also recognized his lifetime work with the worst career achievement award. Boll is the "worst living director on Earth," Wilson told CNN. Boll had a sense of humor about his Razzie success. He sent in a video rejection speech from a fake set of Darfur, Sudan, saying the Razzies had ruined his life and he would never be back. The Razzie team is already predicting next year's nominees. A few to watch out for: "Hannah Montana," "Friday the 13th" and "Bride Wars," -- the last of which has already grossed more than $50 million. "It's kind of like watching a train wreck, isn't it?" Wilson said.

LOS ANGELES, California (CNN) -- It was a night for neon pink bow ties and words such as "disaster" and "monstrosity." It was decidedly not, however, a night to be Paris Hilton, Mike Myers or Uwe Boll.

Paula Einstein, Rebecca Marcotte and Kelie McIver performed a parody of "Dancing Queen" to open the show.

The 29th Annual Golden Raspberry Awards honored the year's worst cinematic achievements at a small theater in Hollywood on February 21. The evening opened with a parody of the "Mamma Mia" song "Dancing Queen" and concluded with "Love Guru" being crowned worst picture.

"It wasn't just the economy that tanked; so did the quality of the movies being offered," Razzie founder John Wilson told CNN several weeks before the ceremony. "I would suggest putting away all sharp [instruments] before putting the DVDs in your machine."

Paris Hilton and Mike Myers emerged on top -- or, more fittingly, at the bottom -- of the awards. Hilton claimed both the worst actress and worst supporting actress honors for her roles in "Hottie & the Nottie" and "Repo: The Genetic Opera." She was also named worst screen couple for her on-screen chemistry with co-stars Christine Lakin and Joel David Moore.

Razzie host Gretchen Enders remarked that "Hottie & the Nottie" was "a vanity production in the worst sense... Hilton, who served as executive producer, has no one to blame but herself." Hilton's film boasted a budget of $2 million yet earned a mere $27,000 at the box office.

"Under Obama's new plan, they wouldn't even have to pay taxes," Wilson deadpanned.

Myers added the worst actor award to the worst picture and worst screenplay Razzies collected by "Love Guru." To spare anyone else the ordeal of watching it, Wilson shredded a DVD copy of the film on stage.

The parody films "Disaster Movie" and "Meet the Spartans," each nominated in five categories, came away empty-handed. This is not to suggest, however, that the Razzie foundation deemed them worthwhile.

"When you invest the kind of money that a mainstream, big-budget star film requires, you want some assurance that your investment is going to come back to you. So... you're going to do what worked before," Wilson said. "Financially, that may make sense, but in terms of the audience's enjoyment, surprise or appreciation of what you're doing, it doesn't work."

Consider "Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull," this year's recipient of the worst prequel, remake, rip-off or sequel award. "A fourth installment of a beloved franchise, but this one found itself loved by almost no one," hosts Katsy Chappell and Josh Thoemke observed.

The approximately 740 voting members of the Raspberry Foundation also found Pierce Brosnan's singing voice sorely wanting. His role in "Mamma Mia" earned him the worst supporting actor award. "An actor who could not sing, should not sing and arguably did not sing, in a role he should not have accepted," Razzie hosts Chip Dornell and Kelie McIver said of the former James Bond.

Yet perhaps the evening's greatest "winner" was Uwe Boll. Not only did he receive the worst director award, but the foundation also recognized his body of work with the worst career achievement honor. Boll is the "worst living director on Earth," Wilson told CNN.

Boll took his Razzie success in good humor. He submitted a video rejection speech filmed on a mock set of Darfur, Sudan, declaring that the Razzies had ruined his life and that he would never return.

The Razzie team is already forecasting next year's nominees. A few to watch out for: "Hannah Montana," "Friday the 13th" and "Bride Wars" -- the last of which has already grossed more than $50 million.

"It's kind of like watching a train wreck, isn't it?" Wilson said.

Both Paris Hilton and Mike Myers dominated -- or perhaps bottomed out at -- the awards. On top of that, she claimed worst screen couple honors for her scenes alongside co-stars Christine Lakin and Joel David Moore.

According to Razzie host Gretchen Enders, "Hottie & the Nottie" represented "a vanity production in the worst sense... Hilton, who served as executive producer, has no one to blame but herself." The movie was made on a $2 million budget yet brought in roughly $27,000 in ticket sales. "Under Obama's new plan, they wouldn't even have to pay taxes," Wilson quipped dryly.

Myers, meanwhile, picked up worst actor to go along with the worst picture and worst screenplay Razzies handed to "Love Guru." In an effort to spare others the experience, Wilson fed a DVD of the film through a shredder on stage.

The parodies "Disaster Movie" and "Meet the Spartans," which each landed five nominations, both went home without any trophies. That said, the Razzie organization hardly considered them worthwhile. "When you invest the kind of money that a mainstream, big-budget star film requires, you want some insurance that your investment is going to come back to you. So... you're going to do what worked before," Wilson explained. "Financially that may make sense, but in terms of the audience's enjoyment, surprise or appreciation of what you're doing, it doesn't work."

That brings us to "Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull," which took this year's prize for worst prequel, remake, rip-off or sequel. As hosts Katsy Chappell and Josh Thoemke put it, "A fourth installment of a beloved franchise, but this one found itself loved by almost no one."

The Raspberry Foundation's roughly 740 voters were also unimpressed by Pierce Brosnan's vocal abilities. His performance in "Mama Mia" landed him the worst supporting actor award. Razzie hosts Chip Dornell and Kelie McIver said of the former James Bond, "An actor who could not sing, should not sing and arguably did not sing, in a role he should not have accepted."

Yet the evening's most decorated "champion" may well have been Uwe Boll. Beyond capturing the worst director trophy, he was honored by the foundation with the worst career achievement award for his body of work. Wilson described Boll to CNN as the "worst living director on Earth."

# Los Angeles, California

Los Angeles, often abbreviated as LA, is the largest city in the state of California and the second-most populous city in the United States. Located in Southern California along the Pacific coast, this sprawling metropolis is known for its year-round pleasant climate, diverse culture, and iconic landmarks.

## The Entertainment Capital

Los Angeles is world-renowned as the heart of the American entertainment industry. Home to Hollywood, the city serves as the center of the film and television world. The famous Hollywood Sign, perched on the hills, has become a global symbol of dreams and stardom. Major film studios, including Universal, Paramount, and Warner Bros., call this city home, attracting aspiring actors, writers, and filmmakers from around the globe.

## Attractions and Culture

The city offers countless attractions for visitors and residents alike. From the sandy beaches of Santa Monica and Venice to the upscale shopping district of Rodeo Drive in Beverly Hills, there is something for everyone. Art enthusiasts can explore the Getty Center and the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA), while families enjoy nearby theme parks like Disneyland and Universal Studios.

## Diversity and Population

Los Angeles is a true melting pot, boasting one of the most ethnically diverse populations in the world. This diversity is reflected in the city's vibrant neighborhoods, delicious cuisine, and rich cultural festivals. Communities such as Koreatown, Little Tokyo, and Olvera Street celebrate the many cultures that make LA unique.

## Climate and Lifestyle

The Mediterranean climate of Los Angeles is one of its greatest appeals, featuring warm, dry summers and mild winters. This sunny weather encourages an outdoor lifestyle, with residents enjoying hiking, surfing, and countless recreational activities throughout the year.

## Conclusion

Los Angeles, California, remains a dynamic and influential city that captivates millions of people. Whether for its entertainment industry, cultural richness, or beautiful landscapes, LA continues to be a destination of endless opportunity and excitement.
